title: SLA and Queue Management
text: Cases approaching service-level limits should be prioritised using queue ageing, bottleneck ownership and hand-off timestamps. Repeated delays should trigger process redesign rather than manual escalation alone.

title: Right-First-Time Quality
text: High rework rates indicate upstream quality or requirements problems. Teams should identify the earliest repeatable defect source, standardise checks and measure first-pass yield after corrective action.

title: Process Handoffs
text: Excessive handoffs increase cycle time and failure risk. Simplify ownership, remove duplicate approvals and automate low-risk transitions where control requirements allow.

title: Automation Governance
text: Automation candidates should be repetitive, rules-based and measurable. Controls must include exception handling, auditability, ownership, rollback and post-deployment monitoring.

title: Data Quality Controls
text: Missing, inconsistent or delayed data should be monitored at source. Critical fields require validation rules, ownership, lineage and exception reporting before downstream analytics are relied upon.

title: Operational Incident Management
text: Recurring incidents require root-cause analysis, clear remediation owners and verification that the fix reduces recurrence. Severity, customer impact and control risk should guide prioritisation.
